result:
I've noted this question and saved the two sources I checked. Here's my answer.

Neither five nor ten: **start with one agent.** More agents don't always give better results, and they can make them worse.

Say a student wants laser cutter time. Your assistant checks their training, then the calendar, then books a slot. Each step depends on the one before. If you split these across agents, they have to hand that information along, and details can get lost.

[Google Research tested 180 setups](https://research.google/blog/towards-a-science-of-scaling-agent-systems-when-and-why-agent-systems-work/). On a planning task where steps depended on each other, every multi-agent version did 39–70% worse than one agent. On a financial analysis task that could be divided into parallel parts, a version with a coordinating agent did about 81% better. These aren't makerspace tests, but I'd expect booking to resemble the first case.

Cost matters for your budget too. [Anthropic reports](https://claude.com/blog/building-multi-agent-systems-when-and-how-to-use-them) that in its testing, multi-agent systems typically used 3–10 times more tokens (the chunks of text that model usage is measured in) for equivalent tasks.

Splitting can pay off when:
- independent subtasks can run in parallel
- irrelevant information from one subtask crowds the model's input and hurts its work on another
- specializing demonstrably helps, such as when one agent struggles to choose among many tools

For your design review, you could say: "We start with one agent, test it on real student requests, and split only if we find a problem that splitting addresses." The number of agents should follow from that evidence.

**Your turn:** which is the better candidate for splitting: searching three separate manuals to compare machines, or the training, calendar and booking sequence? Why?

I can turn this into a short lesson if you like. Context and memory is still next in my notes and will help with the second reason for splitting. Your two quiz 0001 attempts also haven't been graded yet, so just ask when you want that done.
